adults.title: More of His Light, One Day at a Time
adults.big_idea: Jesus Christ is the light and the life of the world, and we receive more of His light as we daily build faith in Him, study the scriptures, and repent.
adults.objective: Learners will name one place in their life where they need the Savior’s light and choose one daily practice from Elder Lebethoa’s talk to invite that light this week.
prepare: Read Elder Lebethoa’s talk, especially the story of the first disagreement and the three things we can do.
Write on the board: Faith in Jesus Christ. Scriptures daily. Repentance daily.
Bring slips of paper and pens for silent writing.

segments.name: When a conversation goes wrong
steps: Begin with prayer. You might sing or read the words of “Come unto Jesus.”
Tell the class that Elder Thabo Lebethoa of the Seventy said many of us have had a conversation with a spouse, child, friend, colleague, or neighbor that did not end as we hoped.
Ask everyone to think silently of one such moment. No one needs to share details.
Ask the question below and take two or three brief answers.
questions: In the hour after a conversation like that, what do you most need?

segments.name: A verse that turned on the light
steps: Retell the story: Elder Lebethoa’s name means joy, and his wife’s middle name means eternal or endless. Shortly after they married, a discussion became their first serious disagreement, then an argument, then the silent treatment.
Explain that while he pondered what to do, the Savior’s words to the people of Nephi came to his mind.
Read 3 Nephi 11:29–30 in pairs. Ask pairs to find what the Savior says is not His doctrine and what is.
Share that Elder Lebethoa said these words enlightened his mind and helped him know how to resolve the challenge, and that this enlightenment comes from the Savior. Read 3 Nephi 11:11 together.
questions: When has a verse of scripture come to mind and shown you what to do next?
Why do you think the Savior’s light and a spirit of contention cannot stay together for long?

segments.name: The answer is always Jesus Christ
steps: Read aloud the list of concerns Elder Lebethoa named: becoming self-reliant, demands at school or work, feelings of inadequacy, fear, and doubt, the loss of a loved one, or simply knowing what to do with our lives.
Invite each person to write on a slip of paper one place where they need more light right now. They keep the slip; no one will read it.
Read the key quote that begins “Whatever concerns” and the one that begins “Jesus Christ can bring light.”
Discuss the question below. Help the class notice that Elder Lebethoa does not say the problem disappears; he says the Savior brings light and restores hope.
questions: What is the difference between having a problem solved and having light in the middle of it?

segments.name: Three ways to receive more light
steps: Divide into three groups, one for each phrase on the board. A small class can take them one at a time together.
Faith group: read Alma 7:11–12 and Doctrine and Covenants 6:36. Share President Oaks’s words from the aligned quotes about daily trying.

Scripture group: retell the man who, after reading the Book of Mormon, took a shovel, dug a hole in his garden, and buried a newly purchased large tin of coffee. Read the key quote about consistency and sincerity.
Repentance group: share Elder Lebethoa’s teaching that repentance means a change of mind and a turning of the heart to God, and read Sister Runia’s words from the aligned quotes.
Give groups four minutes with the questions below, then ask each group for one insight in a sentence or two.
questions: What did Elder Lebethoa teach that makes this practice feel possible rather than heavy?
What has this practice looked like on an ordinary day in your life?

segments.name: Ponder a change
steps: Read Elder Lebethoa’s invitation from the invitations list. Mention the areas he suggested: how we use our time, the things we watch or listen to, and the language and tone we use with others.
Give two full minutes of silence. Ask learners to turn over their slip and write one change to make and one daily practice from the board that will help.
Remind them of his assurance that we do not need to go through this alone. The Savior is always ready to help.
questions: What is one thing the Lord would have you change this week, and which daily practice will you start with?

segments.name: A new day
steps: As a check for understanding, ask one or two people to say in a sentence how we receive more of the Savior’s light.

Share Elder Lebethoa’s promise: he testified that today can be a new day and tomorrow will be a better day for all who come unto Jesus Christ and receive His light. Read Matthew 11:28 and bear your own testimony.
Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking what they noticed when they kept their daily practice.

key_quotes.text: Whatever concerns, challenges, and struggles we may have in our lives, the answer is always Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ can bring light in our moments of darkness and restore hope where there is hopelessness.
Ultimately, the method, timing, and length of our scripture study matter less than the consistency and sincerity of our effort.
It is important to remember that we do not need to go through this alone.

scriptures.use: Read in pairs after the story of the disagreement. Find what the Savior says is not His doctrine and what is.
Read together to see how the Savior describes Himself, and connect it to the way His words enlightened Elder Lebethoa’s mind.
The faith group reads it and lists what the Savior took upon Himself and why. Refer to verse 12 again during the silent pondering.
Read aloud at the close as the Savior’s own invitation, just before you testify.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: strong faith requires more than strong desire. It means daily trying, one step at a time, with prayer and scripture study

aligned_quotes.speaker: Sister Tamara W. Runia
aligned_quotes.text: the invitation to repent is an expression of God’s love. Saying yes to that invitation is an expression of ours

invitations.text: Let us ponder about the changes that we need to make in our lives

takeaways: Jesus Christ is the light and the life of the world.
His light grows in my life through daily faith, daily scripture study, and daily repentance.
I do not have to change alone; the Savior is always ready to help.
act: Put your slip of paper where you will see it each morning and do the one daily practice you chose.
Study the scriptures every day this week at a time that fits your circumstances, even briefly, and watch for one verse that shows you what to do.
Before your next hard conversation, read 3 Nephi 11:29–30 and pray about your language and tone.
Each night, ask yourself what you need to change, and ask the Savior for help with it.
adapt: At home: skip the groups. Talk through the three practices together and let each person choose one for the week.
Large class: let neighbors form the three groups by rows, and take only one insight from each practice.
Short on time: keep the story, 3 Nephi 11:29–30, and the silent pondering. Mention the three practices from the board.

youth.title: Turn Up the Light
youth.big_idea: Whatever we are facing, the answer is always Jesus Christ, and we can increase His light in our lives by daily faith, daily scripture study, and daily repentance.
youth.objective: Youth will explain three ways to receive more of the Savior’s light and commit to one small daily action for the next seven days.
prepare: Read Elder Lebethoa’s talk and mark the three things we can do.
Ask youth to bring their scriptures, on paper or on a phone.
Bring three sheets of paper, each headed with one word: Faith, Scriptures, Repentance.
Be ready to dim the room: lights off or blinds closed.

segments.name: Lights down
steps: As youth sit down, dim the room and turn on one phone flashlight at the front. Ask everyone to find 3 Nephi 11:11 and try to read it.
After a few seconds, invite everyone with a phone to turn on its flashlight. Read the verse aloud together, then turn the lights back on.
Ask the question below, then have someone offer an opening prayer.
Explain that Elder Thabo Lebethoa of the Seventy taught how to receive more of the Savior’s light, and today the class will test his three answers.
questions: What changed in the room, and who changed it?

segments.name: The silent treatment
steps: Retell the story: Elder Lebethoa’s name, Thabo, means joy. His wife’s middle name means eternal or endless. Together their names mean eternal joy. Then, shortly after they married, came their first serious disagreement, an argument, and the silent treatment.
Say that while he pondered what to do, the words of Jesus Christ in the Book of Mormon came to his mind.
Have pairs read 3 Nephi 11:29–30 and decide on one sentence that sums up what the Savior teaches there.
Share that he said these words enlightened his mind and helped him know how to resolve the challenge.
questions: Where do arguments start for people your age: at home, at school, in a group chat?
When has something from the scriptures come to your mind right when you needed it?

segments.name: Is that answer too simple?
steps: Read the list of concerns Elder Lebethoa named: becoming self-reliant, demands at school or work, feeling inadequacy, fear, and doubt, losing a loved one, or simply knowing what to do with our lives.
Give one minute of silent writing. Each person writes, in a private note on their phone or on paper, one thing that feels dark or unclear right now. No one will see it.
Read the key quote that begins “Whatever concerns” and the one that begins “Jesus Christ can bring light.”
Ask the questions below honestly and let youth answer honestly. Point out what he actually promises: light, hope, and a Savior who knows where we have been, where we are, and where we need to be.
questions: Some people hear “the answer is always Jesus Christ” and think it sounds too simple. What do you think Elder Lebethoa means by it?
What is the difference between Jesus Christ removing a problem and Jesus Christ bringing light into it?

segments.name: Three teams, sixty seconds
steps: Form three teams and give each one sheet: Faith, Scriptures, or Repentance.
Faith team: read Alma 7:11–12 and Doctrine and Covenants 6:36, and use President Uchtdorf’s words from the aligned quotes about the tree of faith.

Scriptures team: retell the man who read the Book of Mormon, then took a shovel, dug a hole in his garden, and buried a newly purchased large tin of coffee. Use the key quote about consistency and sincerity, and Elder Lebethoa’s list of ways to study: in order, by topic, with a question, or starting with a verse that draws your attention.
Repentance team: use his teaching that repentance means a change of mind and a turning of the heart to God, and his reminder that we do not need to go through this alone. Read Alma 7:12.
Give four minutes to prepare a sixty-second pitch that answers: What did he teach? What is one thing a teenager could really do this week?
Hear the three pitches. Let the class vote, not for their own team, on the most doable idea.
questions: Which of these three is easiest for you right now, and which is hardest? Why?

segments.name: My seven days
steps: Read Elder Lebethoa’s invitation from the invitations list. Name the areas he suggested: how we use our time, the things we watch or listen to, and the language and tone we use as we communicate with others. You might add that for youth this can include texts and comments.
Read the second aligned quote, from President Uchtdorf at this conference, and say that small is fine.
Give two minutes of silence. Each person writes next to their earlier note: one change I need to make, and one small thing I will do every day for seven days.
Invite two or three volunteers to share only their daily action, not the change.
questions: What time of day will you do it, and what will remind you?

segments.name: A better tomorrow
steps: Check for understanding: go around the room quickly and have each person name one of the three ways without repeating the person before.
Share his promise: he testified that today can be a new day and tomorrow will be a better day for all who come unto Jesus Christ and receive His light. Read Matthew 11:28 and bear your testimony.
Tell the youth that next week you will ask who kept their seven days and what they noticed. Close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: Whatever concerns, challenges, and struggles we may have in our lives, the answer is always Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ can bring light in our moments of darkness and restore hope where there is hopelessness.
Ultimately, the method, timing, and length of our scripture study matter less than the consistency and sincerity of our effort.
Through Him, today can be a new day and tomorrow can be a better day.

scriptures.use: Find and read it during the opening, first by one light and then by many. Ask what the Savior calls Himself.
Read in pairs after the story of the disagreement. Each pair sums up the Savior’s teaching in one sentence.
The Faith team reads both verses and the Repentance team reads verse 12. Look for what the Savior experienced and why that means He can help.
The Faith team reads it and builds its sixty-second pitch around what the Lord asks us to do with our thoughts, doubts, and fears.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf
aligned_quotes.text: Strong faith in Jesus Christ doesn’t happen overnight. No, in this mortal world, it’s the thorns and thistles of doubt that grow spontaneously. The healthy, fruitful tree of faith requires intentional effort

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Uchtdorf
aligned_quotes.text: Spiritual growth is rarely dramatic at the beginning.

invitations.text: Let us ponder about the changes that we need to make in our lives

takeaways: Whatever I am facing, the answer is always Jesus Christ.
I can increase His light by daily faith, daily scripture study, and daily repentance.
Small and consistent matters more than long and impressive, and I am not doing it alone.
act: Do your one small daily action for seven days in a row and note each day what you noticed.
Choose one way to study the scriptures this week, such as by topic or with a question, and keep the same time each day.
Before you answer a message or a person when you feel angry, pause and remember 3 Nephi 11:29–30.
Each night, ask in prayer what you need to change, and ask the Savior to help you with it.
music: Teach Me to Walk in the Light
adapt: At home or with two or three youth: skip the teams. Take the three ways one at a time and let each person suggest one doable idea.
No phones or a room that will not darken: use one flashlight and a single set of scriptures passed along a row, or simply ask when a small light made a big difference.
Short on time: do the opening, the story with 3 Nephi 11:29–30, and the seven-day plan.

children.title: Jesus Christ Is the Light
children.big_idea: Jesus Christ is the light, and I can let more of His light into my life.
children.objective: Children will say that Jesus Christ is the light and show three things they can do to let in more of His light: trust Him, read the scriptures, and try again when they make a mistake.
prepare: Bring a flashlight and a blanket or thick towel.
Bring paper and crayons for each child.
Bring a copy of the Book of Mormon to hold up.
Plan to dim the room a little. Do not make it fully dark.

segments.name: Sing and gather
steps: Sing the song Teach Me to Walk in the Light and have a child pray.
Ask the question below and let several children answer.
Say: Today we will learn who gives us the best light of all.
questions: When it is dark, what helps you see?

segments.name: The light under the blanket
steps: Dim the room a little. Turn on the flashlight and cover it completely with the blanket. Ask if the light is still on.
Let a child lift one corner of the blanket. Let another lift more. Then take the blanket off.
Say: The light was shining the whole time. We let more of it in.
Tell the children that Jesus said, “I am the light and the life of the world.”
Teach the one short truth and repeat it together three times, first in a whisper, then in a normal voice, then standing tall: Jesus Christ is the light.
questions: What happened each time we lifted the blanket?

segments.name: Elder Lebethoa’s story
steps: Tell the children: Elder Lebethoa is a Church leader from South Africa. His name, Thabo, means joy.
Say: One evening he and his wife disagreed. They became upset and stopped talking to each other. Have the children fold their arms and turn away without a sound.
Hold up the Book of Mormon. Say: Then he remembered words Jesus spoke in the Book of Mormon. Jesus does not want us to be angry with each other.
Say: Those words were like a light in his mind. They helped him know what to do. Have the children turn back, unfold their arms, and smile.
questions: How did the words of Jesus help Elder Lebethoa?

segments.name: Three ways to let the light in
steps: Stand in a circle. Teach three actions. Trust Jesus: hands on heart. Read the scriptures: hands open like a book. Try again: turn all the way around and face the front.
Explain each in one sentence. I trust that Jesus knows me and will help me. I read the scriptures and learn about Jesus. When I make a mistake, I turn back to Jesus and try again, and He helps me.
Call out the three ways in mixed order, faster and faster, while the children do the actions. Shine the flashlight on the ceiling each time they get one.
Let a child be the caller for a round.
For the scripture action, hold up the Book of Mormon and share Elder Morgan’s words from the aligned quotes.

segments.name: Draw the light
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Help them fold the paper into three parts.
Ask them to draw a bright light at the top and, in the three parts, themselves trusting Jesus, reading the scriptures, and trying again.
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about one of their pictures.

segments.name: Pass the light
steps: Sit in a circle with the room dimmed a little. Pass the flashlight from child to child.
Whoever holds the light finishes this sentence: This week I can let in the light of Jesus by…
Help any child who is unsure by pointing to their drawing. Thank each child.
questions: Which of the three ways will you try first?

segments.name: A new day
steps: Say the truth together one more time: Jesus Christ is the light.

Tell the children that Elder Lebethoa promised that for everyone who comes to Jesus Christ and receives His light, today can be a new day and tomorrow will be a better day. Share your own testimony in a sentence or two.
Ask the children to take their drawing home and show someone the three ways. Tell them you will ask next week what they did.
Sing the song Jesus Wants Me for a Sunbeam if time allows, and close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: Jesus Christ can bring light in our moments of darkness and restore hope where there is hopelessness.
Through Him, today can be a new day and tomorrow can be a better day.
the answer is always Jesus Christ

scriptures.use: Say the Savior’s words about being the light during the flashlight activity. An older child can read the first part of the verse aloud.
Hold up the scriptures during the game and explain in your own words that God’s word is like a light that shows us where to walk.
At the close, tell the children that Jesus invites everyone to come to Him. Older children can find and read the verse.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Morgan
aligned_quotes.text: No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon.

takeaways: I can trust Jesus, read the scriptures, and try again.
Jesus helps me, and tomorrow can be a better day.
act: Show your drawing to someone at home and teach them the three actions.
Read or listen to a verse from the Book of Mormon each day this week.
When you feel upset with someone, stop, remember Jesus, and use kind words.
When you make a mistake, pray, turn back to Jesus, and try again.
music: Teach Me to Walk in the Light
Jesus Wants Me for a Sunbeam

adapt.younger: For ages 3–7, keep the room mostly light and let every child have a turn lifting the blanket. Repeat the short truth often and play the action game twice instead of adding speed. In the drawing time, ask for one picture only: me and the light of Jesus. A helper can sit beside children who need one.
adapt.older: For ages 8–11, have a child read 3 Nephi 11:11 aloud and another read Matthew 11:28. Let an older child lead the action game. Ask a harder question: Why do you think reading the words of Jesus helped Elder Lebethoa know what to do? Invite them to write one sentence under each drawing about what they will do this week.
